question: Does the measure-consistent training convention (the defect-1 cure) by itself change the zero-shot foreign-family detonation of drive-linear checkpoints?

known_state.historical: Every linear flagship checkpoint detonated to 1e3-1e15 pressure rel-L2 zero-shot on SHIFT-SUV under the fixed gauge; the degree-1 homogeneous mode improved medians ~6700x but with a 2491x seed band (2.07 to 5157).
known_state.new_fact: The four fresh checkpoints (1 control + 3 mixedres, all linear-mode, all measure-consistent) were trained under a convention no historical detonation was measured under; their zero-shot behavior is unknown.

instrument: recipe infer.py, dataset shift_suv_estate_surface (val split, 99 cases; test splits stay sealed), sampling_resolution 10000, the dataset yaml's declared gauge convention unchanged; per-case pressure relative L2 and pred_rms/true_rms from saved predictions
arms: the four defect-1 final checkpoints, zero-shot (no adaptation)

deciding_gates.S1_scorecard_smoke: pressure rel-L2 finite AND < 3.0 on all 4 checkpoints (the frozen scorecard's boundedness axis)
deciding_gates.S2_level_report: no threshold; report per-checkpoint levels and the band (descriptive, feeds stage-1 design)

predictions.S1: p ~ 0.3 that all four pass: the detonation mechanism (drive/coordinate scale excursion) is largely disjoint from the measure axis, but the H-MS unification argued a shared component and the defect-1 result showed the measure convention is more load-bearing than believed
predictions.note: either outcome shapes stage 1: pass -> the homogeneous-mode question becomes incremental robustness and seed-band reduction; fail -> stage 1 tests the homogeneous x measure-consistent conjunction against the unchanged detonation

stage_1_commitment: stage 1 (pre-registered separately after this reads out) trains the homogeneous-mode conjunction at 5 seeds regardless of S1; only its predictions and comparison baseline depend on this result
